package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware campaign, not a public package)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a multi-stage malware loader that uses heavy obfuscation, anti-analysis, and persistence techniques to deliver and execute a variety of remote access trojans (RATs) and stealers, including VenomRAT, NanoCore, XWorm, Remcos, and a crypto wallet stealer. It leverages phishing, script-based loaders, and evasion mechanisms to compromise Windows systems, exfiltrate sensitive data, and maintain long-term unauthorized access.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ECMAScript in SVG: creates a new blob, uses window.URL.createObjectURL to drop a ZIP file (INV0ICE_#TBSBVS0Y3BDSMMX.zip)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the SVG, the script decodes embedded base64 data and writes a ZIP file to disk, enabling further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: SVG files are not expected to drop executables or ZIP files; using ECMAScript for file creation is highly abnormal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SVGs are static images, not executable droppers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, SVGs may use scripts for interactive graphics, but never for file dropping.

execution_context.trigger: user executes batch file from ZIP
execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated batch file (from ZIP, created by BatCloak)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Batch file copies PowerShell executable to C:\Users\Public\xkn.exe, decodes payload to pointer.png, hex-decodes to pointer, moves to C:\Users\Public\Libraries\pointer.cmd, executes pointer.cmd, deletes all files.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the batch file copies and renames PowerShell, decodes and writes a secondary payload, executes it, and deletes traces to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batch files with obfuscated payloads, file copying, and self-deletion are classic malware loader behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate batch files do not obfuscate payloads or delete themselves after execution.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Batch file with junk strings, two Base64 payloads, AES-CBC decryption, GZIP decompression, PowerShell command: [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load([byte[]]...), invokes entry point.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script decrypts and decompresses embedded payloads, loads a .NET assembly in memory, and invokes its entry point to execute malware code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: In-memory assembly loading and obfuscated payloads are advanced evasion and malware delivery techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts do not decrypt and execute .NET assemblies from memory.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Checks for admin privileges, copies itself to %AppData%/strt.cmd or StartUp folder, creates scheduled task 'OneNote 83701' for persistence, loads embedded resource 'P' (VenomRAT), invokes entry point.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes persistence via scheduled tasks or startup folder, then loads and executes VenomRAT from an embedded resource.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication, privilege checks, and scheduled task creation are classic persistence mechanisms for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not covertly install itself for persistence or load RATs from resources.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Patches AMSI scan buffer and EtwEventWrite to bypass AMSI and ETW.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code disables Windows security features (AMSI, ETW) to evade detection and monitoring.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing AMSI and ETW is a hallmark of sophisticated malware seeking to evade security products.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code does not patch system security mechanisms.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Base64/AES-CBC encrypted config, C2 communication, initial packet with hardware specs, username, OS, camera, AV, etc. Encrypted C2 sessions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT collects system and user information, then sends it to the C2 server over encrypted channels.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of system and user data to remote C2 is a core RAT behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not send detailed system info to unknown servers.

execution_context.trigger: VenomRAT plugin handling (save_Plugin directive from C2)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Decompresses plugin DLL from C2, saves to registry, loads and executes plugin payload (e.g., keylogger, stealer).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT receives plugin DLLs from C2, stores them in the registry, and executes them to extend malicious functionality.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic plugin loading from C2 and registry storage is highly stealthy and modular.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not receive and execute code modules from C2 via registry.

execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated VBS file, downloads from hxxps://nanoshield[.]pro/files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VBS downloads JPG with steganographically embedded Base64 malware, decodes to .NET executable, sets HKCU\...\Run for persistence, downloads further payloads, executes via RegAsm.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script downloads and decodes a hidden payload, establishes persistence, and executes NanoCore RAT.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Steganography, registry persistence, and remote payload execution are advanced malware techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not use steganography or execute hidden RATs.

execution_context.file_location: VBS file xwrm3.1.vbs, batch script, PowerShell from hxxps://kisanbethak[.]com/K/Universallsningen.lpk

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell script with junk comments, uses Process Hollowing to inject shellcode into legitimate process, executes XWorm.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script injects shellcode into a legitimate process to execute XWorm, evading detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process hollowing is a well-known malware evasion and injection technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not inject shellcode into other processes.

execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated VBS script remcos.vbs, ScrubCrypt, Guloader PowerShell

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: RC4-encrypted configuration in SETTINGS resource, decrypted and used to configure Remcos RAT.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script decrypts configuration and launches Remcos RAT for remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypted configuration and remote control are classic RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not decrypt and execute RATs.

execution_context.file_location: .NET executable (obfuscated with SmartAssembly), resource file 'ach', scheduled task 'Nano'

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Decodes payload from resource, writes to memory, copies itself to TEMP, sets scheduled task 'Nano' (every 10 min), DLL with Base64 config, monitors for crypto wallets, Foxmail, Telegram, exfiltrates to markjohnhvncpure[.]duckdns.org.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the stealer persistently monitors for sensitive data (wallets, mail, Telegram), collects and exfiltrates it to C2.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated data theft and exfiltration, persistent scheduled tasks, and targeting of crypto wallets are clear indicators of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not steal or exfiltrate user data.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers SVG attachment with embedded malware dropper.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens SVG, ZIP file is dropped.

attack_chain.action: User extracts and executes obfuscated batch file from ZIP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Batch file decodes and executes ScrubCrypt loader.

attack_chain.action: ScrubCrypt batch file decrypts and loads .NET assembly, establishes persistence, and loads VenomRAT.
AMSI and ETW bypasses are applied to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware executes without interference from security tools.

attack_chain.action: VenomRAT collects system info and communicates with C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: C2 can send further plugin payloads.

attack_chain.action: VenomRAT receives and executes plugins (keylogger, stealer, RATs) from C2, storing them in registry.
Plugins (NanoCore, XWorm, Remcos, Stealer) are executed, establishing further persistence, stealing data, and enabling remote control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration, system compromise, and long-term persistence.

behavioral_signatures: SVG or image files with embedded scripts that drop executables or ZIPs
Batch files with heavy obfuscation, payload decoding, and self-deletion
Scheduled task creation with suspicious names (e.g., 'OneNote 83701', 'Nano')
Steganographic payload delivery (malware hidden in images)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for SVG/image files with embedded scripts that create ZIP/executable files. Flag batch files with obfuscated payloads, self-deletion, or PowerShell-based in-memory .NET assembly loading. Detect creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious names and registry-based persistence. Watch for AMSI/ETW patching, process hollowing, and steganographic payload extraction. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains and on exfiltration of system/user data to external servers.
